answer: An agent market serving an inlet port, a terrace farm, and an atlas publisher requires each bidding identity to lock $100 for 30 days. Each bond permits only one active bid, so splitting one agent into a thousand identities creates no free bidding power: the attacker must lock $100,000 to run them all. The delay prevents recycling the same funds across identities, making a sybil swarm costly in capital and lost liquidity.
